subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: Should OpenClaw protect Feishu direct-message sessions with a TTL-aware retention rule and add Feishu-owned malformed open_id repair, or should it only document per-account-channel-peer as the supported multi-account workaround?
rationale: The remaining fix changes durable session retention and identity-validation behavior, and could either grow session stores or split existing direct-message history without a maintainer-approved migration policy.

options.title: TTL-aware direct-DM protection plus repair
options.body: Protect recent human direct-message sessions, keep old one-off DMs prunable, and add Feishu validation or doctor repair for malformed direct keys.

options.title: Blanket-protect direct DMs
options.body: Prevent direct-message eviction entirely, accepting larger stores for bots with many one-time direct senders.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Keep per-account-channel-peer as the supported multi-account path and leave maintenance and malformed-key behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: TTL-aware direct-DM protection plus repair
recommendation.body: Protect recent human direct-message sessions, keep old one-off DMs prunable, and add Feishu validation or doctor repair for malformed direct keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core session-maintenance behavior where steipete has the clearest provenance, while Feishu-specific details should still involve the plugin owner signal.
